Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City DATE: TIME'. OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY DILG Opinion No. 17 S. 2011 MAY 17 2011 MAYOR GENEVIVE G. LIM Caluya, Antique Dear Mayor Genevive G. Lim: This has reference to your letters requesting APPROVAL FROM THIS DEPARTMENT regarding the following: a. b. Transfer the earnings of Barangay Semirara, Caluya, Antique to a private bank. The funds, which are currently maintained in Land Bank of pertain to the proceeds of the Barangay from the the Philippines, mining operations of the Semirara Mining Corporation; and Use a portion of the 80% of the proceeds derived from mining operations (national weatlth) to be invested in Barangay Development Programs. Acting on your first query, please be informed that approval need not be secured from this Department. Per Circular Letter dated 14 March 2006 issued by the Bangko Sentral Ng Pilipinas (BSP), "Provincial, City, and Municipal Treasurers, Commissioners of BIR and BOC, Heads of attached agencies of the DOF, and Head of all Government-Owned and/or Controlled Corporations (GOCCs) are required to secure prior DOF approval if they are to deposit their funds or maintain depository accounts with banks other than the Land Bank of the Philippines and the Development Bank of the Philippines." This was contained in the Bureau of Local Government Finance (BLGF) Memorandum Circular No. 27-2009, copy of which is attached for your reference. Anent your second query, the DILG-DOE Joint Circular No. 98-01 dated 30 September 2008 provides that the utilization of the 80% of the national wealth proceeds shall be applied solely to LOWER THE COST OF ELECTRICITY in the local government unit where such a source of energy is located. This is a mere reiteration of Section 294 of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991. The aforesaid joint circular further provides that "any use of the national wealth proceeds outside the prescriptions in the DILG-DOE Circular No. 95-01 and 98-01 shall require the approval of the DILG Secretary". Section 294 of RA 7160 is explicit on the utilization of the proceeds from the share that is, to finance local of national wealth of the local government units development and livelihood projects, provided however, that at least 80% of the proceeds derived from the development and utilization of hydrothermal, geothermal, and other sources of energy shall be applied SOLELY to LOWER THE COST OF ELECTRICITY in the local government unit where such a source of energy is located.

Page 12 Semirara Mining Corporation is the only large-scale coal producer in the Philippines and is engaged in surface open cut mining of thermal coal from its Panian mine on the Semirara Island in Antique. Clearly, the corporation's activity pertains to the utilization and development of a source of energy. The prohibition in Section 294 of RA 7160 therefore applies. The law does not give the DILG Secretary any discretionary power to alter the law. Your request is to use the remaining balance of PhP 37.2 Million which forms part of the 80% of the proceeds derived from the activities of Semirara Mining Corporation. We regret to DENY such a request for reasons abovestated. Thank you very much. Very yours, AU ERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary for Local Government
